why: Source: minutes per unit for the two periods, read the step chart for four options, four divisions, compare against the baseline with the crossed-threshold trap (about 8 steps); question: the same sequence on a step chart with 45-service steps, same threshold-crossing trap (about 8 steps).

Source: five labelled-bar differences divided by their bases, then rank against options sharing a first entry (about 6 steps); question: the identical five percentage decreases and ranking (about 6 steps).

Source: add two cells for the right line, divide by the right wage while ignoring the distractor wage, pick the largest option that fits (3 steps plus trap); question: the same sum, division, distractor wage and option check (3 steps plus trap).

Source: two baseline minutes-per-unit figures, four step-chart readings and divisions, compare to baseline (about 8 steps); question: the same two baselines, four readings and divisions and a comparison, with a seven-step chart that reads the same way (about 8 steps).

Source: combined total, then gridline-read weighted shares for four statements, two of which fall to the between-the-shares bound (about 4 to 5 steps); question: combined total and four weighted-share checks, of which only the water one falls to the bound (about 5 to 6 steps), so the gap is at most one.
Source: pick the right pie among four, sum three slices, multiply by the sample share (3 steps); question: the same pie selection, three-slice sum and multiplication (3 steps).

Source: test four statements of the same kinds (revenue sum, highest cost, loss comparison, cost estimate) using loss = revenue x margin and costs = revenue x (1 + margin) (about 5 steps); question: the same four statement types and formulas (about 5 steps), only the true one is now the revenue sum.

Source: two baseline minutes-per-unit figures, four step-chart readings and divisions, compare, threshold-crossing trap (about 8 steps); question: the same work with 150 hours and a seven-step chart, the trap now being output just past a jump (about 8 steps).

Source: sum the five indirect segments while ignoring the totals, apply to GDP (2 steps plus trap); question: the identical sum of five indirect segments and multiplication by GDP (2 steps plus trap).

Source: read four gridline values on two axes, two share divisions, difference, divide by three years (about 8 steps); question: the same four dual-axis gridline readings, two divisions, difference and annualising (about 8 steps).

Source: one-time visitors = people x fraction, divide by visits rather than people (2 steps plus trap); question: the same multiplication and division with the same visits-versus-people trap (2 steps plus trap).

Source: test four statements (revenue sum, highest cost, loss comparison, cost estimate) using loss and cost formulas built from the margin (about 5 steps); question: the same four statement types and formulas, with the revenue sum true (about 5 steps).
